claim: On the synthetic_forecast task (timeseries domain, 32-step sine window, 1-step horizon, noise sigma 0.1), the pinned arm digital/feedforward/instantaneous/null/gradient/adam reaches a validation MAE of at most 0.100 at the L2 schedule (5 seeds x 20 epochs) — at least 1.15x below the 0.11459 naive last-value ruler and removing at least 42% of the headroom between that ruler and the 0.07979 irreducible noise floor.

ruler.name: naive last-value forecast (y_hat = x[-1])
ruler.split: synthetic_forecast validation split (n = 994 contiguous windows, 20% tail hold-out)
ruler.note: Measured on the split the cell measures. Linear extrapolation is worse (MAE 0.19950), so persistence is the stronger naive arm and the one registered.

noise_floor.name: irreducible error of a deterministic predictor under the generator's Gaussian noise
noise_floor.note: A threshold below this floor is unreachable by construction; 0.100 keeps 0.0202 of slack above it.

decision_rule: Met iff (1) every one of the 5 seeds writes PASS with val_mae <= 0.100, and (2) the one-sided 95% upper confidence bound of the seed mean (t, df=4) is < 0.100. Marginal iff the seed mean is within 1 SE of 0.100. Distance is reported in SEs and as a fraction of the headroom over naive.
pilot_role: Schedule choice, not threshold choice: a 20-epoch / 1-seed pilot this session measured val_mae 0.0907 after the pipeline learned to train a regression target at all. The threshold is derived from the split's naive ruler and the generator's noise floor, both computable without running the arm.
claim_eligibility: L2 records carry 5 achieved PASS seeds, a replay hash, and a normalized metric, so the run's claim-eligible cell count is non-zero.
